Welcome
Kelly Fletcher, Head of School
Welcome to our school website! I hope you manage to take some time to explore what we have to offer and learn at least a little about what Shaftesbury CE Primary School has to offer and help celebrate our achievements.
At Shaftesbury Primary the children are at the centre of what we do every day. Our ethos is focused on inspiration in all areas and is built upon Christian values that underpin our Church of England status.
Our mission comes from the epistle to the Hebrews, 10:24-25:
24 And let us consider how we may spur one another on toward love and good deeds, 25 not giving up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing, but encouraging one another—and all the more as you see the Day approaching.
As a learning community that involves the children, our families and our staff we aim to ensure that we feel safe, loved and then INSPIRED.
At Shaftesbury CE Primary School, INSPIRE, means we:
are Independent, Never give up, Shine, Participate positively, celebrate Individuality, Reach for the stars, Explore and excite.

pageCache.pageTitle: Outdoor Play and Learning - Gold Award! - Shaftesbury CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Outdoor Play and Learning – Gold Award!
Over the past 2 years, Shaftesbury Primary School has been working with a company called Outdoor Play and Learning, also known as OPAL.
OPAL mentors have been working closely with our staff to develop our play curriculum, ensuring that all playtimes are positive, enjoyable and rewarding for all children. OPAL’s vision is that every child in every school has an amazing hour of high-quality play every day – with no exceptions! The children have played an integral role in the OPAL development and have embraced the positive change in playtimes.
Mr Smiley, Mrs Edwards and Mrs Crockett have driven this project forward within school and our final assessment was in the summer term.
We are very pleased to announce the following:
Shaftesbury Primary School has achieved the Gold Award status from OPAL for our dedication to high quality play provision. Playtimes are inclusive, joyful and provide a wonderful variety of types of play for all children to enjoy.
This is a huge achievement for Shaftesbury Primary School, and we are very proud of our GOLD award. In the coming weeks we will be holding a presentation assembly, run by our OPAL mentor, where we will be officially presented with the Gold Award.

Aims/Ethos
At Shaftesbury CE Primary we create an environment where everybody is:
We subscribe to the thinking that none of us can be ready to be the best that we can be if we don’t feel we are safe (physically, mentally and emotionally), loved and INSPIRED.
Our mission comes from the epistle to the Hebrews, 10:24-25:
24 And let us consider how we may spur one another on toward love and good deeds, 25 not giving up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing, but encouraging one another—and all the more as you see the Day approaching.
The epistle was written at a time of great hardship for recently converted Christians and it brought great comfort to them in a time of challenge and adversity.
The letter to the Hebrews was a support to these early Christians, and its themes of practicing stewardship over your spiritual life and your personal relationship with God still speak to us today.
Our mission reflects the need to provide this kind of support to all of our community.
Our values are all about showing courage in supporting each other by practicing koinonia and respect. How our friendships are valued and how our learning underpins the creation and development of the people we are.
In living out our values – we aim to ensure that all our learning community feel safe, loved and inspired so they are ready for their next steps – whatever they may be.
At Shaftesbury CE Primary School, INSPIRE, means that we:
are Independent, Never give up, Shine, Participate positively,
celebrate Individuality, Reach for the stars, Explore and excite.
We actively develop the Growth Mindset across the learning community and see all children and adults as learners together. We work as a team to help everyone be the best that they can be.

Curriculum & Learning
INSPIRE Curriculum 2025
At Shaftesbury Primary School, our curriculum is designed to ensure every child feels safe, loved, inspired and ready for the next step in their educational journey. Rooted in our belief that all pupils—particularly those who are disadvantaged—deserve the highest quality of education and the strongest foundations for future success, our curriculum brings together the Cornerstones Curriculum, its Big Ideas, and our evidence-informed Shaftesbury Primary Teaching and Learning Principles, grounded in the EEF guidance for raising attainment.
Ambitious, Connected and Knowledge-Rich
We provide an ambitious, coherent and knowledge-rich curriculum built around the Cornerstones Big Ideas such as Humankind, Nature, Conflict & Resolution, Community & Culture, and Processes. These concepts allow pupils to build deep understanding, make meaningful connections across subjects, and develop secure knowledge that they can recall, apply and build upon. Learning sequences are carefully planned to ensure progression, enabling pupils to revisit and deepen key concepts over time.
Cornerstone’s Big Ideas
We also use a range of other resources to support the wider curriculum:
Phonics – Read, Write Inc
Maths and Science – White Rose
Writing – The Write Stuff
Handwriting – Teach Handwriting
RE – Emmanuel Project
PSHE/Sex and Relationships Education – SCARF
MFL – Language Angels
Computing – Project Evolve, Teach Computing
Evidence-Informed Teaching Designed to Secure Strong Outcomes
Our teaching is shaped by the EEF’s most effective principles, including high-quality instruction, scaffolding, explicit vocabulary teaching, structured practice, and purposeful feedback. Through our Shaftesbury Primary Teaching and Learning Principles, teachers prioritise:
· Retrieval practice to strengthen long-term memory
· Modelling and explicit instruction to make learning clear and accessible
· Adaptive teaching so all pupils, including those disadvantaged or with SEND, achieve success
· Deliberate vocabulary development to close language gaps
· Assessment for learning to inform responsive teaching
These are our Shaftesbury Primary Teaching and Learning Principles: SHP Teaching and Learning
Inclusive and Aspirational for All
Equity is central to our intent. We commit to identifying and diminishing barriers for disadvantaged pupils by providing targeted support, timely intervention, and high expectations for all. Our curriculum empowers all children to see themselves as capable learners with bright futures, fostering the belief that we all have the potential to succeed in whatever we choose.
Inspiring Experiences That Build Character and Curiosity
Children learn best when they are inspired. Through Cornerstones’ rich projects, immersive experiences and creative approaches, pupils develop curiosity, creativity and confidence. We enrich learning with visits, visitors, cultural experiences and community engagement so that every child develops the knowledge, skills and personal qualities they need to thrive academically, socially and emotionally throughout their learning journey.
Take a look at some of the enrichment activities the children have enjoyed: Inspiring Experiences
Phonics and Early Reading
At Shaftesbury CE Primary School we use Read Write Inc. to teach phonics all through EYFS and KS1. Each class is assessed and split into small groups so that children are taught within the appropriate phase. Assessment is continuous and children will be moved between the groups as they are ready. Children are taught how to break down words into their individual sounds in order to read and how to put sounds together for writing. Some children in LKS2 will continue to be taught within these phonics groups (stage appropriate). UKS2 children requiring extended phonics input receive Fresh Start phonics intervention.

SEND
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities
School Information Report
‘Our vision for children with special educational needs and disabilities is the same as for all children and young people – that they can achieve well in their early years, at school and in college, and lead happy and fulfilled lives.’ (Department for Education)
Like all children that attend Shaftesbury CE Primary School, we have high aspirations for children identified as having special educational needs or a disability. We ensure that all children are well supported to achieve their full potential. The SENCo works closely with parents or carers, and other professionals to ensure children have the provision they need to progress academically and thrive socially.
Our school prides itself in its ability to offer and successfully deliver a full curriculum that is inclusive to all children, irrespective of need. The SENCo works very closely with all of the teaching staff and, as a result, is able to support children with a wide range of academic, physical and social needs. This may be in the form of classroom based support or withdrawn support, often in small group or one-to-one sessions using resources from within the school and from other support services.
The school and the governing body regularly reviews its provision for children with special educational needs or a disability to ensure that its staff are well prepared and trained. If you would like to discuss any issue regarding your child and Special Educational Needs and Disability, please contact Mrs Edwards: senco@shaftesburyprimary.co.uk who will be happy to provide information and support.

pageCache.pageTitle: NSPCC Number Day - 6 February 2026 - Shaftesbury CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
NSPCC Number Day – 6 February 2026
NSPCC Number Day was a fun and engaging day for all our pupils! Children spent the day exploring maths in exciting ways across different subjects and real-life contexts.
Throughout the day, students took part in a variety of hands-on activities, from solving puzzles and challenges to applying their maths skills using scientific methods, more creative projects, and even everyday scenarios.
This approach helped them see how maths is not just a classroom subject, but something we use all the time in our daily lives. Everyone enjoyed the mix of learning and fun, and it was wonderful to see so many pupils actively engaging with numbers, problem-solving, and teamwork.

pageCache.pageTitle: Rugby Festival - Shaftesbury CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Rugby Festival
On Wednesday 4th February, 17 children from years 5 and 6 represented Shaftesbury Primary in the Shaftesbury Primary Family tag rugby festival. We entered two teams, and the event started with the children taking part in 4 practice activities that were lead by the host’s, Shaftesbury School, sports leaders. The five teams in attendance then took part in a round-robin tournament, with points being awarded for wins and draws.
Some super play from both Shaftesbury teams saw tries galore, and some fantastic team work in both attack and defence. In each game that they played, the players improved their individual and team play, and as a result we finished in 3rd and 4th places in the league.
Congratulations to all players, many of whom were representing our school for the first time.

pageCache.pageTitle: Author visit - Shaftesbury CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Author visit
The Year 3/4 students had a truly wonderful and inspiring day meeting and working alongside Lanisha Butterfield, the amazing author of ‘Flower Block’. The children were completely engaged as Lanisha shared her love of storytelling and reading, sparking thoughtful discussions and creative ideas throughout the sessions.
Prior to her visit, the students were tasked with writing persuasive letters to Lanisha explaining some of the current challenges around reading in our school, while also reflecting on the potential benefits of her visiting and working with them. Through this experience, the children were able to see those benefits come to life, as meeting a real author, hearing her story, and learning alongside her helped make reading feel exciting, meaningful, and fun. It was a powerful experience that strengthened their confidence as readers and writers and has already helped to grow a renewed love of reading across the year group. 📚✨
Congratulations to the winners of the persuasive letter writing competition:

Pupil Premium
Pupil Premium Strategy 2024 – 2027 (including 2025 review)
What is the Pupil Premium?
Introduced in 2011, the pupil premium is a sum of money (additional funding) given to schools each year by the Government to improve the attainment of disadvantaged children. This funding is based on research showing that children from low income families perform less well at school than their peers. Often, children who are entitled to pupil premium can face challenges such as poor language and communication skills, lack of confidence and issues with attendance and punctuality. The pupil premium is intended to directly benefit the children who are eligible, helping to narrow the gap between them and their classmates.
Which pupils receive Pupil Premium funding?
Children who have qualified for free school meals at any point in the past six years. The school receives £1320 for each of these children. Children who are or have been looked after under local authority care for more than one day. These children are awarded a premium of £2300. Children from service families who receive a child pension from the Ministry of Defence. These children are awarded £300. Principles:
Through Quality First Teaching, we aim to ensure that teaching and learning opportunities meet the needs of all pupils. We ensure that appropriate provision is made for pupils who belong to vulnerable groups, this includes ensuring that the needs of socially disadvantaged pupils are adequately assessed and addressed. In making provision for socially disadvantaged pupils, we recognise that not all pupils who receive free school meals will be socially disadvantaged. We also recognise that not all pupils who are socially disadvantaged are registered or qualify for free school meals.
Reporting and accountability:
It is the responsibility of the Inclusion Leader/Deputy Headteacher to produce regular reports for the school governors. The reports should focus on measuring the effectiveness of the pupil premium approach and spending against its impact on disadvantaged children compared with non-disadvantaged nationally. We are committed to meeting the needs of all pupils, whether or not they are eligible for the Pupil Premium.
Other ways we can support:
Shaftesbury CE Primary School has considered how to use the pupil premium funding they receive to support eligible children. If your child is eligible for funding, then you could receive support as follows:
Please note: this offer cannot be used more than once per academic year.
To be eligible you must be in receipt of one of the following benefits:
Income Support Child Tax Credit, provided you are not entitled to Working Tax Credit and have an annual taxable income that does not exceed £16,190 Income-Based Job Seekers’ Allowance Employment Support Allowance (Income Related) Guaranteed Element of State Pension Credit Support under Part VI of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999
If you think you may be eligible, please visit the Dorset Council website. It is easy to apply and you are told immediately if you are eligible. If you have any questions or queries, please contact the school office who will be happy to assist you.
